title: Literature check ~17:45Z: droplet predator-prey (Meredith 2020) is a variant of the food chain; the conserved-enzyme consumer has no direct precedent; saturable-gain soliton theory (Akhilesh & Gat 2026) bears on the CGLE line
summary: Opened 5 primary abstracts. Meredith et al. 2020 show chasing between droplets that transfer oil from prey to predator, without reproduction or a regrowing resource, so c42's food chain is a variant; c43's consumer, conserved and condensing only by catalysis on prey, has no direct precedent in what I opened. Saha et al. 2020 (nonreciprocal Cahn-Hilliard) is the operator that could make consumers hunt between meals. Akhilesh & Gat 2026 treat slow saturable gain for dissipative solitons; c43's CGLE gain world is a variant and their drift result motivates a global-gain test. Zwicker et al. 2017 remains the nearest work for dividing fuel-made droplets.
